starts without this one's messages.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC notes: boundary domino rays / opposed panels

## Verified rule from task-90f4638b (2026-10-20)

A large uniform-background field contains a matching 2-cell domino at a boundary and a lone interior colored cell. The domino is a directional emitter: use the column/row of its first cell (for the horizontal dominoes in these examples, the left cell) and draw inward, perpendicular to the domino, through the background using the lone cell's original color. Preserve the domino. If the ray encounters the lone cell in its path, recolor that lone cell to 4 and stop the ray there (do not paint past it). A ray that does not encounter it continues to the opposite boundary.

Evidence:
- Demo 1: 7-background 7x16. Horizontal 8 domino at top row cols 14-15; second at bottom row cols 9-10. Lone 3 at (row 3,col 9). Output has 3 down col14 from row1 through row6; 3 up col9 at rows4-5; lone 3 becomes 4; pairs unchanged.
- Test solved: 9-background 22x18. Top horizontal 0 pair at row0 cols3-4; bottom pair at row21 cols16-17; lone 1 at (5,3). Accepted output: color1 fills col3 rows1-4, lone cell becomes 4; color1 fills col16 rows1-20; both 0 pairs and all other 9s unchanged.

Important correction: collision cell is always 4 in these examples, not the next color and not 2. Rays use the singleton's original color. On a collision, stop before/at the singleton (the singleton itself is 4), and leave beyond it untouched.

## Related panel pattern from demo 2

In a two-panel arrangement separated by a row/column boundary, sparse markers in one panel can produce full stripe(s) in the opposite panel at corresponding offset indices. In the 25x12 demo, the divider is row12. Markers in lower-panel rows 13,14,16,17,18,23 correspond to upper rows 1,2,4,5,6,11 respectively (row offset from divider); those upper rows are filled with marker color 9 across the panel. In the lower panel, each marker 9 changes to 4 and paints 9 horizontally toward the right boundary, preserving other cells and boundary 7s. Treat as a potentially related, distinct configuration; the boundary-domino ray rule above is the directly relevant verified rule for the solved test.
